transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Alex Li (Redwood Product), Emily Rodriguez (NovaSearch Head of Search), Mike Chen (CTO), Priya Singh (Data Engineer)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranker endpoints for improving search relevance. Customer currently on Elastic + homegrown reranker; wants better recall and rerank without huge infra lift. Discussed experiment plan and pilot benchmarks.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint, batch reranking, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, SSO), sample benchmark plan, next steps for POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Sara with Redwood, AE for the accounts in EMEA and NA. Quick intros?
[00:08] Emily: Hi, I'm Emily, Head of Search at NovaSearch. We've got Priya and Mike on the call as well.
[00:12] Mike: Hey all.
[00:13] Priya: Hi!
[00:15] Daniel: Daniel here, I'm the solutions engineer. We'll walk through hosted embeddings and the rerank endpoint and show a couple quick demos in the console and API.
[00:25] Sara: Goal for today is to see how our embeddings + rerank could slot into your existing Elastic pipeline and what a small pilot would look like.
[00:32] Emily: Yep, our main ask is better relevance. Right now we index with Elastic for recall and use a custom BERT reranker for top-100; that's expensive and slow. Latency is a problem for interactive search.
[00:44] Priya: We also want to measure MRR gains and keep cost reasonable. We're concerned about hosted data retention and compliance.
[00:52] Daniel: Totally. We'll show hosted options and some controls—token retention settings, and the Dedicated/private options if you need VPC or on-prem later. For the hosted demo today we'll focus on the API endpoints.
[01:05] [screen share begins] Daniel: First up embeddings endpoint. You send text, you get a vector. We support batching and streaming. Example call in the SDK here - we show a couple of sentences.
[01:20] Emily: Quick Q, do you recommend storing embeddings in our DB or using a vector DB? We currently keep them in Elastic vectors.
[01:28] Daniel: If Elastic is working for you for nearest-neighbor recall, you can keep it and call our embeddings endpoint to generate vectors. The rerank endpoint can accept a candidate list of doc ids + embeddings and do relevance scoring without moving your whole storage. So hybrid works well.
[01:42] Mike: How does rerank differ from a typical cross-encoder? Is this a separate model call?
[01:47] Daniel: Good question—our rerank endpoint is a lightweight reranker optimized for production. It accepts query + list of documents (text or embeddings) and returns reordered list with scores. Under the hood it's tuned for latency/cost tradeoffs; it's not necessarily a full cross-encoder like a huge BERT but it's tuned to give large MRR improvements while keeping token costs low.
[02:10] Priya: Do you support batch reranking? We have to rerank hundreds of queries for evaluation.
[02:14] Daniel: Yes, there's a batch rerank mode you can call via API. It accepts up to X candidates per request and we can stream results back. For offline evals we can do large batches via the batch job API. We'll include sample scripts.
[02:28] Emily: Latency numbers? Interactive search target is <200ms tail when possible.
[02:33] Daniel: For hosted small rerank calls we typically hit 50-150ms p95 depending on candidate size and sequence length. If you need stricter SLOs you can go Dedicated or tune batching/cache. These numbers are based on our verified model profiles but every workload differs.
[02:47] Emily: Sounds promising. Cost — how do we estimate token costs vs running our own BERT?
[02:53] Alex: We provide unit economics tooling in the Console and Optimize toolkit. It shows token cost per rerank call and suggests quantized model variants or batching to reduce unit price. For pilots we usually do a 2-week benchmark and share a cost spreadsheet.
[03:08] Priya: We already saw Pinecone and Algolia in evaluations. Any notes on vendor lock-in?
[03:12] Sara: We try to be flexible—open model catalog and you can export vectors. The idea is minimal lock-in: we handle serving and reranking but you own your raw data.
[03:21] Mike: Security—SOC2? SSO? KMS?
[03:24] Sara: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we support SAML SSO and RBAC, and KMS integrations for private deployments. For hosted we have configurable retention and audit logs; for higher security we offer Private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed KMS.
[03:41] Emily: Good. For pilot we probably need the hosted path but with stricter retention and audit settings.
[03:47] Daniel: That's straightforward. We'll propose a hosted pilot with tightened retention and write the pilot plan into the SOW.
[03:54] [Daniel shares live demo: console showing embeddings job, rerank playground]
[04:05] Daniel: Here in the Console you can drop in a query and a few docs and see rerank scores. You can also upload a CSV of query-candidate pairs for batch scoring.
[04:20] Priya: The UI is handy. Can we integrate this into our current pipeline as a microservice?
[04:24] Daniel: Yes, the API is simple REST/SDK. We have client libs in Python and Node. Example flow: 1) call embeddings endpoint, 2) nearest-neighbor in Elastic, 3) call rerank endpoint with top-K documents for final ordering.
[04:41] Emily: How do you handle prefix/KV cache? We have recurring queries and want to avoid recomputing heavy context.
[04:47] Daniel: We support KV/prefix caching for prompt-like workflows; for rerank specifically, caching embeddings or using persistent vector store avoids recompute. Our SDK and Console show cache hit rates in the Optimize tab.
[05:03] Mike: Any gotchas with doc lengths or tokenization variance?
[05:06] Daniel: Very long docs should be chunked; sequence length impacts latency and cost. Our model selection and kernel paths try to optimize for that, but chunking and smart candidate selection matter.
[05:18] Emily: Ok let's talk pilot acceptance criteria. We want a measurable MRR uplift on our dev set and p95 latency under 300ms for rerank.
[05:27] Sara: Sounds good. Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: run baseline with current reranker, run Redwood rerank on same candidate set, compare MRR/latency/cost. We'll do a 1k query benchmark as a starting point.
[05:40] Priya: We'll share sample dataset and existing evaluation scripts.
[05:43] Emily: Timeline—if we can kick off next week, we'd like results by mid-November.
[05:49] Sara: We'll follow up with a pilot SOW and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:52] [brief crosstalk about calendar times and timezone]
[06:05] Daniel: A couple quick notes—if you want to avoid moving vectors to a new DB, you can post candidate IDs with embeddings inline and we score them server-side. That keeps your Elastic as the source of truth.
[06:18] Mike: Is there rate limiting on the hosted API we should know about for the pilot?
[06:21] Daniel: We have sensible defaults and can temporarily raise limits for pilot customers; we can also set per-route quotas.
[06:29] Emily: Ok that addresses most of our concerns. Any final questions?
[06:33] Priya: One last thing—how do we measure regression risk, e.g., precision drop on certain queries?
[06:38] Alex: We recommend A/B testing and also Redwood's quality monitoring to tie regressions to specific prompt sets and evals. We'll include a suggested eval suite in the follow-up.
[06:51] Sara: Recap of next steps: Sara sends pricing and pilot SOW, Daniel runs the 1k-query bench once Priya shares data, Priya shares dataset and current eval scripts, schedule POC scoping for week of 2026-10-26.
[07:05] Emily: Great, thanks everyone.
[07:08] Mike: Thanks.
[07:10] Sara: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the docs and action items.

End of transcript.
